title: Three Nights and One Short Score
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：orchestra　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 orchestra 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1989 the musician ① led the orchestra that no listener in the hall would have counted, and he said the leading was the whole of the night. The ② orchestra, meaning the band itself and not the score, ran three nights and stayed uncounted in the book; an orchestra, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ orchestra in that hall had the same short score beside it, and the ④ orchestra at the far piano, meaning the note they kept for the children to play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An orchestra, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the musician said the counting is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the orchestra was the whole of the matter, meaning the harmony and not the band. The ⑥ orchestra, meaning the harmony and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; orchestra, he said, is either something you lead or the only word that means both a band and a harmony. He said the harmony is the part they remember.

By 1994 the ⑦ orchestra had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short score. The ⑧ orchestra of the whole thing, the musician wrote in December, was one hall and three nights of counting; orchestra, he said, is either the note at the far piano or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ orchestra I remember is the band counted in the programme, which closed in 1996 and is still counted as the quietest in the hall. An ⑩ orchestra, my mother said in 1998, is the only band that improves by being counted; every orchestra, she said, is a harmony that has agreed to look like a band. She said the harmony was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 管弦乐队（指音乐厅里每一支旁边的那一支）
B. n. 管弦乐队（指那支管弦乐队本身，与薄薄的乐谱相对）
C. 固定搭配：lead the orchestra 指挥这一支管弦乐队
D. n. 管弦乐队（指留给孩子们弹的那一个）
E. n. 管弦乐队之事（抽象总称，指一处音乐厅的管弦乐队之事）
F. n. 管弦乐队（指节目单里写到、被清点的那一支）
G. n. 管弦乐队、和谐（指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 和谐（抽象总称，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: led the orchestra that no listener in the hall would have counted
The orchestra, meaning the band itself and not the score
the orchestra at the far piano
the orchestra was the whole of the matter
the orchestra had become a line in a programme
The orchestra of the whole thing
An orchestra, my mother said in 1998

answers.why: lead the orchestra 意为“指挥这一支管弦乐队”，1989 年那位乐师把音乐厅里没有一位听客肯清点的一支管弦乐队做了一遍。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队”，指那支管弦乐队本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被清点。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队”，指音乐厅里每一支旁边的那一支，每一支旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队”，指最远那张琴凳的留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队、和谐”，指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这支和谐就是那件事的全部。
orchestra 意为“和谐”，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西而不是那支管弦乐队，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队”，指节目单里写到、被清点的那一支，到 1994 年这一支成了节目单里的一行。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队之事”，乐师十二月写道，整件事的管弦乐队之事是一处音乐厅和三个夜晚的清点。
orchestra 意为“管弦乐队”，我记得的是节目单里清点过的那一支，1996 年奏完了，至今仍被说成音乐厅里最安静的一支。
orchestra 为抽象总称，母亲 1998 年说，管弦乐队是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的管弦乐队。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1989 年那位乐师指挥了音乐厅里没有一位听客肯清点的一支管弦乐队，他说这一遍才是那个夜晚的全部。（lead the orchestra）
那支管弦乐队，指的是那支管弦乐队本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被清点。（orchestra）
那处音乐厅里每一支管弦乐队旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。（orchestra）
最远那张琴凳那支管弦乐队，指的是他们留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（orchestra）
叔叔说这支和谐就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那支管弦乐队。（orchestra）
1998 年母亲说，管弦乐队是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的管弦乐队。（orchestra）

My uncle said the orchestra was the whole of the matter, meaning the harmony and not the band.
